_why_one_subtree_rule_and_where_it_lands: **Where the tree keeps `Contribution` was read, not assumed.** The AmigaOS
3.9 CD carries a `Contribution` drawer at its own root - it is one of the
three directories `media_artefacts_adopted.json` records for that disc -
but **no component of `amigaos-3.9.json` copies it**: `workbench-base` and
`workbench-39` between them place `OS-VERSION3.9/WORKBENCH3.5/*` and
`OS-VERSION3.9/WORKBENCH3.9/*`, and neither names `Contribution` (checked
against the recipe on 2026-09-08). So a tree ART builds has no
`Contribution` drawer at all, and this rule creates one.
`Contribution/BoingBag3.9-2` rather than `Contribution` itself: the disc's
own contribution and this BoingBag's are two different collections of
somebody else's programs, and merging them into one drawer would put the
update's ClassAction on top of the disc's the day somebody teaches
`workbench-base` to place the disc's drawer. Beside it, never over it.
**The icons ride with the files.** A `subtree` rule copies every entry
below `from`, and 64 of the 445 entries are `.info` files - the drawer
icons for `Contribution`, `ClassAction`, `OpenURL` and `cddb-lib` among
them. That is how `locale-39`'s own subtree rules already carry theirs;
nothing here treats `.info` specially, and nothing has to.
`BoingBag3.9-2/Contribution.info` and `BoingBag3.9-2.info` sit *above* the
rule's `from` and are deliberately not placed: an icon for a drawer whose
destination name is different would name the wrong thing.
_why_overrides_is_empty: Measured rather than defaulted. `Contribution/BoingBag3.9-2` is a
destination no shipped component writes - no release recipe places a
`Contribution` drawer at all (above), and no other package does either -
so there is nothing for this to be replacing. Declaring an override that
names no real collision is ART-159's own mistake, and an empty list here
is the measured answer rather than the unexamined one.
